biodiversity_overview.text: 230,657 GBIF occurrence records for 93 tracked species are attributed to Kerala, spanning 1830-2026.
223,749 of these records (97.0%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 25, Magnoliopsida 19, Mammalia 16, Actinopterygii 10, Amphibia 8, Squamata 6, Testudines 4, Cephalopoda 2, Crocodylia 1, Pinopsida 1, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 10 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN), Tiger (EN), Sloth Bear (VU), Mugger Crocodile (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Mango (49,615), Indian Gooseberry (19,533), Indian Scimitar-Babbler (16,693), Indian Golden Oriole (14,845), Indian Swiftlet (14,730).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 13,845 in 2016 to 8,068 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 6.53% of Kerala's area (35 areas intersect the state).
8.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (18,301 of 223,749); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Toad-skinned Frog (0.69), Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Courser (0.47), Mugger Crocodile (0.46), Kerala Hills Frog (0.45).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Kerala (equal-weight reference): cell near 11.625N 75.375E (overall rank 13, median rank across weightings 21); cell near 9.375N 76.125E (overall rank 18, median rank across weightings 29); cell near 8.625N 76.875E (overall rank 21, median rank across weightings 28).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 26,675 km2 (70.03% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

1,082.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (4.06% of the 2000 extent; 2.83% in 2015-2024, rank 8 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2023 (125.01 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 3.02% of land and population density is 1,115.7 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
20% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
